en.title: Termination and Dismissal Explained Simply
en.directAnswer: Termination, dismissal, discharge, retrenchment and resignation are not the same legal event. The correct rights depend on why the job ended, the worker’s legal status, notice, misconduct process, length of service and applicable law. Keep the termination letter and do not sign a settlement you do not understand.

atAGlance.whoFor: A worker has lost a job and wants to understand the legal terms.
atAGlance.legalBasis: Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006 as amended by Act No. 43 of 2026; contract law; EPZ Labour Act where relevant.
atAGlance.mainRule: Use the exact legal category from the employer’s document. Do not call every job loss “dismissal.”
atAGlance.updateStatus: Current law changed in 2026. Do not use pre-2026 termination summaries without checking the amended sections.

en.lawMeaning: Use the exact legal category from the employer’s document. Do not call every job loss “dismissal.” This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Check disciplinary process if misconduct is alleged.
evidence: Appointment letter; policies; warning letters; show-cause notice; termination letter; payslips; attendance; settlement.
en.simpleExample: An employer labels a letter “termination” but also accuses the worker of misconduct. The worker should get the legal effect reviewed instead of relying only on the heading.
commonMistakes: Common mistakes: Signing “full and final” without reading.
